Interaction with existing AIOS residency-mask + lazy-TLB scaffolding

findings.title: Operand encoding error in TLBI instructions after ASID-generation implementation
findings.problem: The design (IMPL doc lines 149-151) specifies that invalidateTLBByASID and invalidateTLBByASIDVA must translate the logical seL4 asid to the hardware asid before issuing the TLBI. However, the current code at lines 1106 and 1128 passes the logical asid directly to invalidateTranslationASIDMask/Single, which then encodes it as 'asid << 48' into the TLBI operand. This places the LOGICAL asid in [63:48] instead of the HARDWARE asid. ARM ARM specifies that TLBI aside1/vae1 operands must contain the hardware ASID in [63:48]. If the logical asid and hardware asid differ (as they do under ASID-generation), the TLBI targets the wrong ASID and fails to flush the intended entries. Scenario: Thread A (logical_asid=2, hw_asid=5) unmaps a page; code issues 'tlbi aside1, (2 << 48)' instead of 'tlbi aside1, (5 << 48)'. The entry tagged hw_asid=5 is not flushed. If hw_asid=5 is later assigned to thread B, thread B inherits the stale entry -> cross-process memory access (security hole).
findings.fix: At line 1106, implement the IMPL spec: call 'aios_hwasid_current(asid)' to get the hardware ASID; if it returns 0 (no live entries), return early; otherwise pass the hw_asid to invalidateTranslationASIDMask. Similarly at line 1128 for invalidateTLBByASIDVA. The fix must be conditional on AIOS_ASID_GEN (non-HYP only, since HYP path is untouched). Example: (after line 1105) 'word_t hw_asid = aios_hwasid_current(asid); if (hw_asid == 0) return; invalidateTranslationASIDMask(hw_asid, SMP_TERNARY(aios_asid_residency(asid), 0));'
findings.lens: ARM AArch64 ASID / TCR / TLB architecture - adversarial review of ASID-generation TLB recycling design for AIOS RPi4

findings.title: Missing reserved-ASID mechanism at generation wrap for currently-running vspace
findings.location: seL4/src/arch/arm/64/kernel/vspace.c:98-102 (in aios_hwasid_for), per IMPL doc section 5, open question 1
findings.problem: The generation wrap (when g_hwasid_next > AIOS_HWASID_MAX) issues a full TLB flush (tlbi vmalle1) and resets g_hwasid_next=1. However, if a vspace V is currently running under hardware ASID H at the moment of wrap, the CPU continues to run V after the flush and refills TLB entries tagged H (in the new generation). If g_hwasid_next then climbs back to H and assigns it to a different vspace W before V context-switches away, both V and W will have TLB entries tagged H. Thread W can then speculatively access VA patterns from V's old mappings and hit stale entries from V, causing cross-process data leak. The ARM A72 / BCM2711 may perform aggressive TLB prefetch or L1 cache retention of translated addresses. Scenario with 16-bit ASIDs and 65536 vspaces: (1) Vspace V1 assigned hw=1 in gen=1; (2) 65534 more vspaces assigned hw=2..65535; (3) wrap: gen=2, vmalle1, g_hwasid_next=1; (4) V1 still running on TTBR0[63:48]=1; (5) New vspace V2 assigned hw=1 in gen=2; (6) V1 and V2 both tag entries with hw=1; (7) V2 hits V1's stale entry.
findings.fix: The Linux/xv6 fix (mentioned in IMPL doc section 5, Q1): at wrap time, identify the currently-running vspace on each core (via per-CPU state or inspection of ksCurThread), reserve its hardware ASID, and re-stamp its entry with the new generation using the same hw value, then set g_hwasid_next to skip past the reserved value. This ensures the running vspace keeps its ASID and stale entries tagged with that ASID are not reused until the next wrap (another 65536 assignments). Example code structure: 'if (wrap) { asid_t running_asid = getCurrentVSpaceASID(); word_t reserved_hw = armKSHwAsid[running_asid].hw_asid; ++g_hwasid_gen; tlbi_vmalle1 + remote ipi; armKSHwAsid[running_asid].gen = g_hwasid_gen; g_hwasid_next = reserved_hw + 1; }'
findings.lens: ARM AArch64 ASID / TCR / TLB architecture - adversarial review of ASID-generation TLB recycling design for AIOS RPi4

findings.title: Operand-width assumption: 16-bit hardware ASIDs required, must be verified at boot
findings.location: seL4/include/arch/arm/arch/64/mode/object/structures.bf:11-12 (TCR_ASID16 set by elfloader), IMPL doc section 1, item 2
findings.problem: The ASID-generation design assumes 16-bit hardware ASIDs (TCR_EL1.AS=1, setting bits [63:48] as ASID). If TCR_EL1.AS=0 (8-bit ASIDs), only bits [63:56] are used; the TLBI operand encoding 'asid << 48' would place an 8-bit asid in [63:56] and garbage in [63:57], causing incorrect ASID tagging. With 8-bit ASIDs, wrap happens every 256 assignments, making the wrap-reservation issue (finding 2) much more frequent and critical. The design depends on 'wraps ~never' (IMPL line 28-29), which is only true with 16-bit ASIDs. The elfloader mmu.S reportedly sets TCR_ASID16, but this is not dynamically verified in the kernel.
findings.fix: Add a kernel boot-time assertion: read TCR_EL1.AS and assert it is 1 (16-bit mode). Print an error and halt if it is 0. This must run before any call to aios_hwasid_for. IMPL doc section 6 acknowledges this as 'step 1' of verification plan.
findings.lens: ARM AArch64 ASID / TCR / TLB architecture - adversarial review of ASID-generation TLB recycling design for AIOS RPi4

findings.title: Self-munmap reload sequencing relies on implicit return-path behavior; should be made explicit
findings.location: seL4/src/arch/arm/64/kernel/vspace.c:1178 (unmapPage), section 4 of IMPL doc, lines 189-194
findings.problem: Section 4 of the IMPL design describes the self-munmap path (when unmapPage is called for the currently-running thread's vspace): call aios_hwasid_clear(asid) to mark the hw_asid as stale, then rely on the 'unconditional setVMRoot that the unmap invocation's return path already performs' to reload with a fresh hw_asid. However, the design then notes (lines 191-194) the concern: 'if a path can resume on the SAME H without reload, INV is violated.' And proposes: 'The conservative belt-and-braces: in unmapPage/unmapPageTable, when the asid is current, ALSO do the reload immediately (armv_contextSwitch(curRoot, fresh)), not just clear.' The current code (line 1226) does NOT do the immediate reload for the self-munmap case under ASID-GEN. It relies on the return path, which is implicit and fragile. If a code path can bypass the implicit return-path reload (e.g., a missing setVMRoot, or an optimization in the fastpath), the thread resumes under the OLD hw_asid H, and the just-cleared entry generates a fresh hw_asid binding that competes with H. New mappings added before the reload would have the fresh asid but compete with stale entries tagged H.
findings.fix: Modify unmapPage and unmapPageTable: when asid == current thread's asid, immediately call aios_hwasid_clear(asid), then immediately call armv_contextSwitch(vspace_root, AIOS_HWASID(asid)) to force a fresh hw_asid reload before returning to user mode. Make this unconditional (not deferred) to ensure the reload completes in-kernel while the BKL is held. Verify that all return paths from unmapPage reach this reload.
findings.lens: ARM AArch64 ASID / TCR / TLB architecture - adversarial review of ASID-generation TLB recycling design for AIOS RPi4

findings.title: Multicore coherence of fresh-ASID swaps not fully specified for coresched
findings.problem: If a vspace V is resident (has run) on multiple cores under core-scheduling, and core 0 calls aios_hwasid_clear(V->asid), then assigns a fresh hardware ASID on the next call to aios_hwasid_for, core 1 will still have the old hardware ASID in its stale TTBR0 register (or its thread-local stashed value) until it context-switches. If core 1 resumes running V before re-resolving the fresh ASID, it translates under the old hw_asid and can hit stale entries. The design's residency-mask widening approach (via aios_mark_asid_residency) only widens the mask when a new core runs a vspace; it does not force remote cores to re-sync fresh-asid assignments. The fastpath and setVMRoot always re-call aios_hwasid_for (via AIOS_HWASID macro), so they will pick up the fresh asid on the next load. But if a stale thread-local cache of the hw_asid exists, it could be used.
findings.fix: Under coresched (when CONFIG_MAX_NUM_NODES > 1), ensure aios_hwasid_clear broadcasts a per-core invalidation so each core's cached hw_asid entry is cleared. Or, require that aios_hwasid_for is always called in setVMRoot/fastpath (which it is, via AIOS_HWASID macro), not cached. Verify no per-core stale hw_asid cache exists. For the current core-0-only config, this is moot.
findings.lens: ARM AArch64 ASID / TCR / TLB architecture - adversarial review of ASID-generation TLB recycling design for AIOS RPi4

findings.title: CRITICAL: aios_hwasid_for called from fastpath before vspace.c in unity build, but lacks extern declaration in fastpath.h
findings.problem: The design calls aios_hwasid_for(asid) from switchToThread_fp in fastpath.h (line 40 will be AIOS_HWASID(asid)), but fastpath.h is compiled BEFORE vspace.c in the unity build (per the design doc). The macro AIOS_HWASID(a) expands to aios_hwasid_for(a), which is defined only in vspace.c. Without an explicit 'extern word_t aios_hwasid_for(word_t)' prototype in a header visible to fastpath.h (tlb.h per the design), the fastpath code will have an undefined reference at compile time. The design mentions tlb.h should have the prototype (line 131-132), but fastpath.h line 14 includes armv/context_switch.h, not tlb.h — this is a COMPILE FAILURE risk if the include order is wrong.
findings.fix: Ensure fastpath.h includes <arch/machine/tlb.h> (or a header that includes it) where the AIOS_HWASID macro and aios_hwasid_for extern prototype are defined. The macro definition in tlb.h (lines 129-135 of the design) must be visible to fastpath.h before the switchToThread_fp function uses it. Verify the unity-build include order: fastpath.h must see tlb.h's macro + extern.
findings.lens: Interaction with existing AIOS residency-mask + lazy-TLB scaffolding

findings.title: RACE: aios_hwasid_for wrap+flush side effect can conflict with concurrent TTBR writes from another core
findings.problem: The aios_hwasid_for function performs a global wrap operation (increment g_hwasid_gen, flush, reset g_hwasid_next) as a SIDE EFFECT when called from the fastpath on ANY core. The wrap is unguarded by any lock (the design says 'updated under the big kernel lock' for lazy-TLB, but aios_hwasid_for is called from the fastpath which holds the BKL before and after setVMRoot, but the fastpath ITSELF (switchToThread_fp at line 40) runs WHILE holding the BKL). However, the wrap+flush sequence (lines 98-104) is not atomic: between the check 'g_hwasid_next > AIOS_HWASID_MAX', the wrap, and the reset, another CPU's context switch could call aios_hwasid_for and see g_hwasid_next stale or partially updated. On SMP, if CPU0 is mid-wrap (has bumped g_hwasid_gen and flushed, but not yet reset g_hwasid_next), and CPU1 calls aios_hwasid_for and checks g_hwasid_next > AIOS_HWASID_MAX before CPU0 resets it, CPU1 could wrap AGAIN unnecessarily, or worse, assign a hw asid from the NEW generation while the OLD generation's entries are still live in TLB on CPU0.
findings.fix: Protect the wrap operation (lines 98-104 of the aios_hwasid_for function) with explicit synchronization. Either (a) make the wrap a single atomic operation (not feasible inline), or (b) call aios_hwasid_for ONLY under the big kernel lock (BKL) from the fastpath, or (c) re-check the wrap condition under a spinlock inside aios_hwasid_for. The BKL is held during switchToThread_fp calls from the slow path, but the fastpath may not hold it during ALL its execution — verify. If the fastpath does NOT hold BKL during switchToThread_fp, then aios_hwasid_for CANNOT be called from the fastpath without synchronization.
findings.lens: Interaction with existing AIOS residency-mask + lazy-TLB scaffolding

findings.title: WINDOW: deleteASID Step 2 flushes hw_asid AFTER aios_hwasid_clear, creating incoherence
findings.problem: The Step 2 design says 'deleteASID...STILL call invalidateTLBByASID (now flushing the correct hw asid). Behavior-preserving indirection. Also call aios_hwasid_clear(asid) in deleteASID AFTER the flush'. But the actual code in vspace.c:1247 calls invalidateTLBByASID(asid) first, THEN aios_asid_clear_pending_flush(asid). The design's intent is: flush the hw asid (clearing old entries), THEN abandon the binding (set gen=0) so a future reuse gets a fresh hw asid. However, there is a CRITICAL WINDOW: between the flush (line 1247) and the abandon (line 1251), if another CPU context-switches the SAME sel4_asid before the abandon, that CPU will call aios_hwasid_for which sees gen=current and returns the SAME hw_asid that was just flushed AND is about to be marked as used by this NEW vspace. The old vspace's entries (flushed but not yet fully wiped on all cores due to the remote IPI latency) may still be live when the new vspace runs under the same hw asid on a remote core. This is a STALE TLB HIT vulnerability.
findings.fix: BEFORE calling invalidateTLBByASID, call aios_hwasid_clear(asid) to mark the binding as stale (gen=0). Then call invalidateTLBByASID — which will call aios_hwasid_current(asid), see gen!=current, return 0, and skip the flush (correct, there are no current-gen entries to flush). Then a future vspace that reuses this sel4_asid will get a FRESH hw asid after the global tlb has been flushed at the next wrap. This matches the design intent: 'deleteASID -> no flush; aios_hwasid_clear. A future vspace...gets a FRESH hw asid -- never the dead one's.' Alternatively, in Step 2, do NOT call aios_hwasid_clear until AFTER the flush completes on all cores (but there is no 'after' sync point in the design). The safe path is: clear first, skip flush.
findings.lens: Interaction with existing AIOS residency-mask + lazy-TLB scaffolding

findings.title: ISSUE: Residency shootdown operand changes from sel4_asid to hw_asid, but mask is unchanged; could send IPI to wrong cores
findings.problem: The design changes invalidateTLBByASID to use aios_hwasid_current(sel4_asid) to get the hw_asid, then calls invalidateTranslationASIDMask(hw, residency-mask). The MASK parameter is aios_asid_residency(asid) where asid is still the sel4_asid. But the residency bitmap is indexed by sel4_asid: armKSASIDResidency[asid] stores which cores have run a vspace under that LOGICAL asid number. When the flush operand changes from sel4_asid to hw_asid, there is a semantic mismatch: the residency bitmap says 'cores that have loaded THIS sel4_asid into TTBR0', but the tlbi operand is now 'the hw_asid bound to THIS sel4_asid THIS GENERATION'. If a sel4_asid is re-used by a DIFFERENT vspace WHILE its old hw_asid is still cached on a core, the residency bitmap for that sel4_asid still contains the stale bits (cores that ran the OLD vspace), and the flush targets those cores with the WRONG hw_asid (the old one's). This is BOTH incorrect (flushes the wrong translation) and could miss a core that NOW runs the new vspace under the new hw_asid but is not in the residency bitmap for this sel4_asid yet.
findings.fix: The residency mask MUST be indexed by hw_asid, not sel4_asid, to remain correct after the flush operand changes. Create a parallel hw_asid residency table: armKSHwASIDResidency[hw_asid] (or dynamically compute it from the sel4_asid->hw mapping for cores in the current mask). Alternatively, keep sel4_asid residency but clear it whenever aios_hwasid_clear is called (the hw_asid is abandoned, so the old residency is void). However, this fails in Step 3+ when unmapPage sets a pending flag instead of flushing: the pending flag clears the hw binding but doesn't clear residency, and a future flush of this sel4_asid with a NEW hw_asid will use the OLD residency bits. The safest fix: maintain TWO tables side-by-side for now, or redesign residency to index by hw_asid (requires updating aios_mark_asid_residency to use hw_asid, which it does NOT have access to — it receives sel4_asid from the fastpath). This is a BREAKING change to the residency scaffold.
findings.lens: Interaction with existing AIOS residency-mask + lazy-TLB scaffolding

findings.title: HAZARD: aios_hwasid_clear called from unmapPage's lazy-TLB branch does not prevent concurrent aios_hwasid_for assignment
findings.problem: In Step 3+ (unmapPage non-current -> aios_hwasid_clear instead of pending_flush), when a page is unmapped from a vspace that is NOT currently running, the design calls aios_hwasid_clear(asid) and then later (on the next context switch to that asid) aios_hwasid_for(asid) will see gen=0, assign a fresh hw_asid, and flush. However, between the clear and the context switch, a THIRD vspace could be created that REUSES the same sel4_asid number (ASID pool alloc of a freed slot). That new vspace would call aios_hwasid_for, see gen=0, and assign the NEXT hw_asid value from g_hwasid_next. But the FIRST vspace's old hw_asid (the one cleared) is still in the TLB on cores where it ran — ABANDONED, not flushed. If that first vspace's old hw_asid (say, 42) happens to wrap around and be assigned to the SECOND new vspace before a generation wrap, we have TWO live sel4_asids using the same hw_asid (42), which violates INV. This can happen if g_hwasid_next climbs fast and wraps within one generation.
findings.fix: Assign a NEW hw_asid immediately upon aios_hwasid_clear, don't defer it to the next context switch. Alternatively, ensure that a sel4_asid's hw_asid binding is never reused without a generation wrap + global flush. The current design assumes 16-bit hw_asids make wraps rare, but under high load (many processes) wraps could happen frequently. Add a RETIRED hw_asid list: when aios_hwasid_clear is called, mark that hw_asid as retired for THIS GENERATION and skip it in future g_hwasid_next assignments until the next wrap. This adds complexity (scan a list on every assign), but ensures INV.
findings.lens: Interaction with existing AIOS residency-mask + lazy-TLB scaffolding

findings.title: INCOMPLETE SPEC: aios_mark_asid_residency called in fastpath has no protection against concurrent modify of residency bitmap
findings.problem: The fastpath calls aios_mark_asid_residency(asid) (line 53 of fastpath.h) to set the bit for the current CPU in the residency bitmap. The function (vspace.c:786) does a read-modify-write of armKSASIDResidency[asid]: 'armKSASIDResidency[asid] |= (uint8_t)BIT(cpu)'. This is NOT atomic on ARM64 (ldr-orr-str). If two threads/cores execute this concurrently on the SAME asid (e.g., a vspace is being run on multiple cores simultaneously during coresched), the concurrent updates can lose bits (one thread's OR result gets overwritten by another's). The design claims 'updated only under the big kernel lock' (vspace.c:872), but the fastpath at line 53 runs AFTER the thread context switch is already set (line 63), and at that point other CPUs may also be switching. Under DEFAULT core-0 pinning this is moot (residency[asid] is always {core0}), but for general coresched, this is a data race.
findings.fix: Use atomic operations for residency bitmap updates: atomic_or or __sync_fetch_and_or on the uint8_t armKSASIDResidency[asid] element. Alternatively, assert that the fastpath runs with BKL held (verify the fastpath is protected), or use a per-ASID lock for the residency bitmap (per the existing note that the BKL is sufficient under core-0 pinning).
findings.lens: Interaction with existing AIOS residency-mask + lazy-TLB scaffolding

findings.title: DESIGN QUESTION: Step 2 behavior-preservation claim requires aios_hwasid_clear call before flush to avoid window
findings.problem: The design Step 2 says 'behavior-preserving' but does not clarify the ORDER of operations in deleteASID. The document says 'call aios_hwasid_clear(asid) in deleteASID AFTER the flush', but this creates the window identified in finding #3 (flush THEN clear = stale hit risk). The design's INV statement says 'aios_hwasid_clear(sel4_asid)...next aios_hwasid_for returns FRESH hw asid' but does not specify that the clear must happen BEFORE the flush to be safe under ASID-gen. This ambiguity could lead to implementation error.
findings.fix: Clarify in the design that Step 2 must CLEAR before FLUSHING (order matters), or document that Step 2 accepts the window as a short-term trade-off (stale entries abandoned, will be wiped at next wrap, acceptable under 16-bit asids). Make this explicit in implementation comments.
findings.lens: Interaction with existing AIOS residency-mask + lazy-TLB scaffolding

findings.title: Generation counter wraparound creates live vspace mapping to stale hw_asid
findings.problem: When g_hwasid_gen increments and wraps from 0xFFFF to 0, the code re-stamps it back to 1. However, old entries in armKSHwAsid[] still have .gen=1 from before the wrap. When aios_hwasid_for() checks 'if (e->gen != g_hwasid_gen)' on such an entry (line 97), the condition becomes FALSE (1 != 1 is false), so the function returns the STALE hw_asid instead of assigning a fresh one. If that hw_asid is concurrently issued to a different sel4_asid on another core, a stale TLB hit occurs.
findings.fix: Change line 99 to NOT cycle the generation counter back. Either: (A) use a wider counter (u32 instead of u16) so wrap is astronomically rare and acceptable, OR (B) if wrapping must happen, bump to a DIFFERENT start value (e.g., 'g_hwasid_gen = 2' instead of '1') so old gen=1 entries mismatch. The generation counter should STRICTLY INCREASE or CYCLE to a disjoint value.
findings.lens: multicore/coresched + generation-wrap reserved-asid (classic Linux ASID allocator)

findings.title: Fastpath uses stale cached hw_asid after generation wrap, bypassing resolver
findings.location: fastpath.h:40, section 3 line 145 (design) vs actual code
findings.problem: The fastpath switchToThread_fp() receives 'stored_hw_asid' as a cached value from a prior context switch. After a generation wrap, this cached hw_asid may be stale (generation changed but the stored value wasn't re-computed). The design doc (section 3, line 145) says to call 'armv_contextSwitch(vroot, AIOS_HWASID(asid))', which invokes the resolver. But the actual fastpath code at line 40 uses the raw 'asid' (extracted from stored_hw_asid), NOT passing it through AIOS_HWASID(). This means the fastpath bypasses generation checking and writes a stale hw_asid to TTBR0 after a wrap. The thread then runs under an old hw_asid that may be reissued to a different vspace.
findings.fix: The fastpath MUST call AIOS_HWASID() on the sel4_asid before using it. Since the fastpath does not have direct access to the sel4_asid (only the cached hw_asid), either: (A) store the sel4_asid in the TCB alongside the cached hw_asid and re-resolve on every switch, OR (B) fall back to setVMRoot() on every context switch (sacrificing the fastpath optimization under ASID-gen). The cached hw_asid optimization is fundamentally incompatible with generation tracking.
findings.lens: multicore/coresched + generation-wrap reserved-asid (classic Linux ASID allocator)

findings.title: Self-munmap on multicore vspace lacks cache coherency; stale TLB on peer cores after gen clear
findings.problem: When a thread self-unmaps a page from a vspace that is CURRENTLY RESIDENT on multiple cores (coresched): (1) unmapPage calls aios_hwasid_clear(asid) to abandon the hw_asid binding on core 0. (2) Core 1 is still RUNNING the same vspace in user mode under the old hw_asid with the STALE page in its TLB. (3) Core 0's return path reloads TTBR0 with a fresh hw_asid. (4) But core 1 never receives notification; it keeps running under the old hw_asid. (5) If core 1 refills the TLB entry (miss refill after cache eviction), it re-tags it with the old hw_asid. (6) Later, when the system reissues that old hw_asid to a DIFFERENT vspace, core 1's stale entry becomes a live cross-process hit. INV is violated: two distinct live vspaces share the same hw_asid (old stale binding on core 1, new binding on the new vspace).
findings.fix: Self-munmap must ensure all cores running the vspace are aware of the gen-clear. Send a masked remote IPI (using residency mask) to all cores running the asid after aios_hwasid_clear(), forcing them to re-resolve their TLB on next miss. Alternatively, restrict self-munmap to single-core vspaces only (assert residency has one bit), or implement synchronous reload + IPI-based flush before clearing gen (as hinted in section 4, lines 191-194 of design doc).
findings.lens: multicore/coresched + generation-wrap reserved-asid (classic Linux ASID allocator)

findings.title: Wrap-time reserved-asid logic is designed but not implemented in resolver code
findings.problem: The design doc (section 5.1) requires: 'at wrap, RESERVE every currently-active hw asid (per core) so it is not reissued this generation, and re-stamp the active vspace's entry into the new gen with the same value.' But the provided aios_hwasid_for() code does NOT implement any reservation or re-stamping. On coresched, if core 0 wraps while core 1 runs under hw_asid=1337: (1) wrap increments gen, resets g_hwasid_next=1, (2) no check for active hw_asids on other cores, (3) next aios_hwasid_for() hands out hw_asid=1337 to a NEW vspace, (4) core 1 still runs the OLD vspace under hw_asid=1337 with stale entries, (5) CROSS-PROCESS HIT when the old vspace consults its stale TLB.
findings.fix: Implement the Linux PCID fix: at wrap time, iterate through all cores and scan their TTBR0[63:48] field (or use a per-core 'active_hw_asid' cache) to identify currently-running hw_asids. Reserve these values (mark them as unavailable for new assignment) and re-stamp their entries' generation to the new gen with the same hw_asid value. Only after all active cores have context-switched away can the hw_asid be reclaimed. This is complex and requires per-core state tracking.
findings.lens: multicore/coresched + generation-wrap reserved-asid (classic Linux ASID allocator)

findings.title: Residency mask sticky-wide under dynamic coresched migration causes inefficient IPIs
findings.problem: aios_mark_asid_residency() only sets bits for the current core; never clears them. Under dynamic coresched (vspace runs on core 0, then core 1, then core 0 again), residency becomes sticky-wide {0,1} and remains so until deleteASID(). Teardown IPIs both cores even though the vspace is no longer running on core 1. This is inefficient but not a correctness bug (unnecessary flushes do not corrupt). However, under extreme migration churn, causes performance degradation.
findings.fix: Implement residency narrowing: when a vspace context-switches OUT of a core, clear its residency bit on that core. This requires tracking context-switch-out events in the scheduler, which is non-trivial in seL4. Alternatively, accept the efficiency gap as acceptable under research OS model, since the default core-0 pinning is unaffected.
findings.lens: multicore/coresched + generation-wrap reserved-asid (classic Linux ASID allocator)

result.synthesis:
I have what I need. The design doc resolves several of the disputed points. Now I'll synthesize.

# ASID-Generation TLB Recycling — Adversarial Review Synthesis

I read the IMPL doc and the live `vspace.c:1080-1249`. The 17 raw findings collapse into **7 real issues** plus a handful that the design already pre-empts. I'm ranking by blast radius: a missed flush or a stale-TLB cross-process hit is top; perf/style is bottom. I also flag which step each gates.

## TOP TIER — stale-TLB / cross-process corruption or compile failure (MUST-FIX before any flash)

### M1. The remaining `tlbi`s flush the LOGICAL asid, not the HW asid — STEP 2 blocker
**Where:** `vspace.c:1106` (`invalidateTLBByASID`) and `:1128` (`invalidateTLBByASIDVA`), non-hyp `#else` branch.
**Bug:** Both sites still pass `asid` (logical) straight into `invalidateTranslationASIDMask` / the `(asid<<48)` operand. Once `armv_contextSwitch` writes `AIOS_HWASID(asid)` into TTBR0[63:48], live entries are tagged with the **hw** asid. A flush keyed on the logical asid therefore hits the wrong tag and leaves the real entries live. The instant a hw value is recycled, the next vspace inherits them → cross-process read. This is exactly the case the design calls out in §3 lines 149-152 but the *current code has not applied yet*.
**Fix (per the doc's own spec):** translate first.
```c
/* :1106 */ word_t hw = aios_hwasid_current(asid);
            if (hw == 0) return;                 /* nothing live this gen */
            invalidateTranslationASIDMask(hw, SMP_TERNARY(aios_asid_residency(asid), 0));
/* :1128 */ word_t hw = aios_hwasid_current(asid);
            if (hw == 0) return;
            invalidateTranslationSingleMask((hw << 48) | (vaddr >> seL4_PageBits),
                                            SMP_TERNARY(aios_asid_residency(asid), 0));
```
Note the residency **mask** correctly stays keyed on the logical asid (the bitmap is logical-asid-indexed) — only the **operand** becomes hw. See M-merge below for why that split is fine and the cross-lens "mask is wrong" panic is overstated.
**Gates:** STEP 2. This *is* the "behavior-preserving indirection" — it must be exactly right before anything downstream is trusted.

*(Merges raw findings #1 and #9. The §4-residency-confusion finding (#9) claimed the mask itself must move to hw-indexing; that is wrong for STEP 2/3 under the abandon-don't-recycle rule — see M-merge.)*

### M2. Wrap re-stamp can hand a STALE-but-same-gen hw value to a second vspace — STEP 2+ (algorithm core)
**Where:** `aios_hwasid_for` wrap branch, IMPL §2 line 99.
**Bug:** On wrap, `if (++g_hwasid_gen == 0) g_hwasid_gen = 1;`. The generation is `uint16_t`. After 65534 wraps it cycles back to a value that **already tags abandoned entries** from a much-earlier generation. `aios_hwasid_current`/`aios_hwasid_for` compare `e->gen == g_hwasid_gen`; a stale entry whose `.gen` collides with the recycled live gen reads as *valid*, returns its old hw value, and now two live vspaces can share a hw asid with no intervening flush of *that* binding. INV broken.
**Reality check:** This requires 65534 full wraps, each of which is itself ~65535 assignments — astronomically rare in practice. But the host wrap-stress test (tiny `AIOS_HWASID_MAX`, IMPL §6) **will** drive gen wrap fast and trip this, and it's a one-line correctness fix, so do it now.
**Fix:** Make gen monotonic and wide enough that it never recycles within a boot. Widen `g_hwasid_gen`/`.gen` to `uint32_t` (or `word_t`), drop the `==0 → 1` cycle (keep only `0` reserved as "never assigned"). With a 32-bit gen and a 16-bit hw space, gen exhaustion is ~2^48 assignments = not reachable.
**Gates:** the resolver — STEP 2 (it ships the moment `aios_hwasid_for` is live).

*(Raw finding #11.)*

### M3. Fastpath must NOT cache the hw asid — it must re-resolve through `AIOS_HWASID` every switch — STEP 2 blocker
**Where:** `fastpath.h:40` (`switchToThread_fp`).
**Bug:** Two raw lenses split on this, but they're the same hazard: if the fastpath writes a hw value cached in the TCB from a prior switch, then after a gen wrap (M2) or a self-munmap clear (M5) that cached value is stale — the thread resumes under an abandoned/recycled hw asid. The design's intent (§3 line 145) is correct — `armv_contextSwitch_HWASID(vroot, AIOS_HWASID(asid))` re-resolves every time — but it depends on the fastpath having the **logical** `asid` in hand and calling the resolver, never a stashed hw value.
**Fix:** Confirm the fastpath path extracts the **sel4/logical** asid (from the vspace cap, as the slowpath does) and feeds it through `AIOS_HWASID(asid)` on every switch. Do **not** add a per-TCB hw-asid cache. The resolver is a bounds-check + one compare + (cold) one increment — cheap enough for the fastpath. If for any reason the fastpath cannot get the logical asid cheaply, fall back to `setVMRoot` under ASID_GEN rather than caching hw.
**Also confirm the include/declaration:** `fastpath.h` must see the `aios_hwasid_for` extern + the `AIOS_HWASID` macro from `tlb.h` *before* `switchToThread_fp` uses it (unity-build order). If the include chain (`fastpath.h` → `armv/context_switch.h`, not `tlb.h`) doesn't pull it in, this is a hard compile failure, not a subtle bug.
**Fix the include:** ensure `fastpath.h` includes `<arch/machine/tlb.h>` (or that the macro+extern live in a header already on `fastpath.h`'s path).
**Gates:** STEP 2 (the TTBR write sites change in step 2).

*(Merges raw findings #6 (compile/extern) and #14 (stale cached hw). Both reduce to: re-resolve, don't cache; make the decl visible.)*

### M4. deleteASID: CLEAR the binding **before** the flush, or skip the flush entirely — STEP 2 / STEP 3 boundary
**Where:** `vspace.c:1247` (`invalidateTLBByASID(asid)`), IMPL §3 lines 155-158.
**Bug:** The doc says "call `aios_hwasid_clear(asid)` *after* the flush." That ordering opens a window: flush hw=H on the local core, but the remote IPI flush of H has latency; meanwhile another core could context-switch the same logical asid (still gen=current until the clear lands) and `aios_hwasid_for` hands back the *same* H to what is about to become a different vspace, while remote stale-H entries are still draining. Two live bindings to H momentarily.
**Fix (clean, and it makes STEP 3 fall out for free):** clear **first**.
```c
aios_hwasid_clear(asid);          /* gen=0: H is now abandoned     */
invalidateTLBByASID(asid);        /* aios_hwasid_current -> 0 -> returns early; no flush */
```
With M1 in place, `invalidateTLBByASID` now sees `hw==0` and skips — which is *exactly* the STEP 3 "deleteASID → no flush" behavior. So the safe STEP 2 ordering and STEP 3 are the same code; STEP 2 just hasn't removed the (now-inert) call yet. This dissolves the "behavior-preserving" worry: clearing-first under single-core core-0 pinning changes nothing observable (the dead vspace never runs again), and it's correct under SMP.
**Caveat for STEP 2 "behavior-preserving" claim:** clearing-first means STEP 2 no longer issues the deleteASID `aside1` even on the Pi. If Bryan wants STEP 2 to be *byte-for-byte* the old flush behavior (to isolate the plumbing in the A/B), keep flush-first but **only under single-core core-0 config** where the window cannot open, and document that the SMP-safe ordering (clear-first) lands in STEP 3. Given the default is core-0 pinned, either is safe to flash; clear-first is strictly better.
**Gates:** STEP 2 ordering, becomes STEP 3.

*(Merges raw findings #8 and #12.)*

### M5. Self-munmap clear must be paired with an in-kernel reload on the SAME return path — STEP 4 blocker
**Where:** `unmapPage` current-asid branch (`:1227`) and `unmapPageTable` current (`:1175`), IMPL §4.
**Bug:** Step 4 replaces the eager `tlbi vae1` with `aios_hwasid_clear(A)` and *relies on the return path's `setVMRoot`/fastpath* to reload a fresh H'. If any return path (notably a fastpath restore) resumes the thread without re-resolving, it runs under the old H with the just-removed entry still live — the dominant stall's correctness replacement silently reintroduces a stale hit in the *current* process. The doc flags this as an open question; it must be closed, not assumed.
**Fix (take the doc's own belt-and-braces, make it mandatory):** in the current-asid branch, do the reload **inline**, not deferred:
```c
aios_hwasid_clear(A);
armv_contextSwitch(curVSpaceRoot, AIOS_HWASID(A));  /* assigns fresh H', writes TTBR0, isb */
```
This is self-contained, runs while the BKL is held (no user instruction between unmap and reload — the doc's guarantee holds), and is idempotent across a multi-page unmap: each page clears (gen=0, cheap), the reload at the end consumes it once → one H' for the whole syscall. Then **audit every return-to-user path** (slowpath `setVMRoot`, fastpath restore, fault-reply) to confirm none can resume on stale H even without the inline reload — the inline reload makes it correct regardless, the audit makes it provable.
**Gates:** STEP 4.

*(Merges raw findings #4 and #15 (self-munmap, single-core). The multicore variant is M6.)*

## SECOND TIER — real but coresched-only; MUST-FIX before SMP/coresched, may WAIT under default core-0 pinning

### S1. Wrap-time reserved-asid for the currently-running vspace (multicore) — STEP 2+ on SMP only
**Where:** wrap branch of `aios_hwasid_for`; IMPL §5 Q1.
**Bug:** At a wrap the running vspace keeps executing under its old H, refilling entries tagged H in the *new* gen after the flush. If `g_hwasid_next` climbs back to H this gen and assigns it to another vspace before the runner switches out → stale hit. The doc correctly argues this is **benign under default core-0 pinning** (we wrap in-kernel mid-context-switch, about to load the new vspace's fresh asid; the old runner isn't live), and only bites coresched.
**Fix (Linux PCID pattern, defer until coresched):** at wrap, reserve every per-core active hw asid (re-stamp the running vspace's entry into the new gen with the same H, advance `g_hwasid_next` past reserved values). Requires per-core "active hw asid" state.
**Gates:** correctness on SMP/coresched. The **wrap-stress host test must exercise it** (tiny HWASID_MAX + simulated multi-core residency) even though the Pi default won't hit it — that's the only place it'll surface.

*(Merges raw findings #2 and #16. Both are the same reserved-asid hole.)*

### S2. Fresh-asid swap visibility across cores running the same vspace — coresched only
**Where:** `aios_hwasid_clear` under coresched; IMPL §5 Q2.
**Bug:** vspace resident on cores {0,1}; core 0 clears + reloads fresh H'; core 1 keeps running old H, can refill H, and when H is later reissued → cross-process hit on core 1.
**Why it can WAIT:** default config pins all user threads to core 0 → residency is always {core0}, no peer runs the vspace. Moot today.
**Fix when coresched lands:** on `aios_hwasid_clear` of an asid whose residency mask >1 bit, send a masked remote IPI forcing peers to re-resolve (or restrict self-munmap to single-resident vspaces). The residency mask already widens for genuine coresched, so the targeting data exists.
**Gates:** STEP 3/4 on SMP/coresched.

*(Merges raw findings #5, #10, #13. #13 is the strongest statement of it.)*

### S3. Wrap+flush side-effect from the fastpath has no extra lock — verify BKL coverage
**Where:** wrap branch reached via fastpath `switchToThread_fp`; IMPL §2 lines 98-104.
**Bug:** the wrap (bump gen, flush, reset `g_hwasid_next`) is a global side effect with no internal lock; if the fastpath context-switch can run without the BKL on SMP, two cores can wrap concurrently / read a half-updated `g_hwasid_next`.
**Reality:** seL4 holds the BKL across the whole syscall including the fastpath context switch in the standard config, so this is almost certainly already serialized — **verify, don't assume.** Under core-0 pinning there's only one switching core, so moot today.
**Fix:** confirm the BKL is held across `switchToThread_fp`'s call to the resolver. If a lockless fastpath variant is ever enabled, the wrap must move under a spinlock or be hoisted out of the fastpath.
**Gates:** SMP correctness; verification item, not new code under default config.

*(Raw finding #7.)*

## BOTTOM TIER — already handled by the design, or perf-only (do NOT block on these)

- **8/16-bit ASID width assertion (raw #3):** valid but the design already schedules it as verification step 1 (boot-probe TCR_EL1.AS=1). Keep it — add `assert`/halt before the first `aios_hwasid_for` — but it's a one-liner the doc owns, not a redesign.
- **Residency bitmap RMW not atomic (raw #10, the residency half):** real only under concurrent coresched on the same asid; moot under core-0 pinning (residency is always {core0}). When coresched lands, use `__atomic_fetch_or` on the `uint8_t`. WAIT.
- **Residency mask sticky-wide → extra IPIs (raw #17):** perf, not correctness (over-flushing never corrupts). Acceptable for a research OS; narrowing needs context-switch-out hooks seL4 doesn't have cheaply. DROP for now.

### M-merge note on the "mask must be hw-indexed" claim (raw #9)
One lens argued the residency mask itself must move from logical-asid to hw-asid indexing, calling the split a breaking bug. It is **not**, under the abandon-don't-recycle rule: a logical asid's residency bits describe which cores ever loaded *that logical asid's vspace*. When `aios_hwasid_clear` abandons H and the next resolve assigns H', the **same logical asid** is still the cap identity and still runs the same vspace on the same cores — so the logical-asid-indexed residency mask still correctly names the cores to IPI for that vspace. The hw value never gets reused under a *different* logical asid without a full flush (that's INV). So operand=hw, mask-index=logical is correct. The only place this could break is exactly S1/S2 (coresched wrap/peer visibility), which are tracked separately. No parallel hw-indexed table is needed.

## VERDICT

**Is the core invariant (§1) sound?** Yes. "Each hw value bound to ≤1 live vspace, never reissued without an intervening full flush" is the correct Linux-ASID-allocator invariant and the abandon-don't-recycle + wrap-flush mechanics enforce it — *provided* the resolver never lets a stale `.gen` masquerade as live and the flush operand is the hw value. The two ways the current spec/code can violate INV are M1 (flush keyed on the wrong asid) and M2 (gen counter recycling). Fix those and the invariant holds for the default config.

**MUST-FIX before any HW flash (in priority order):**
1. **M1** — translate logical→hw in `invalidateTLBByASID`/`...VA` with the `hw==0` early-return. Without it STEP 2 is *actively wrong* (flushes nothing real), the worst kind of "behavior-preserving."
2. **M2** — widen the generation counter to 32-bit, drop the `==0→1` recycle. One-liner; closes the only INV hole reachable by the host wrap-stress test.
3. **M3** — fastpath re-resolves via `AIOS_HWASID(asid)` every switch (no cached hw value) **and** the `tlb.h` extern/macro is visible to `fastpath.h`. The include half is a compile gate; the cache half is a correctness gate after wrap.

Plus the **clear-before-flush ordering (M4)** — it's a trivial reorder that makes STEP 2 SMP-safe and turns into STEP 3 for free; bundle it with M1.

**Can safely WAIT (default core-0 pinned config):** M5's inline reload is required *for STEP 4* but STEP 4 isn't this session. S1/S2/S3 and the atomic-residency item are all coresched-only and provably moot under core-0 pinning — but **S1's reserved-asid logic and M2's wrap behavior MUST be covered by the host wrap-stress unit test** (tiny `AIOS_HWASID_MAX` + simulated multi-core residency), because the host test is the only place gen-wrap is reachable; the Pi default will never wrap in a normal A/B.

**One process guardrail:** the design correctly notes QEMU is HYP and cannot exercise any of this — so the host unit test (IMPL §6) is the *primary* proof for M1/M2/M4 and the debug-build per-assign INV scan is the on-HW tripwire for M3/M5. Land both before the Pi A/B; do not treat a green QEMU gate as evidence the ASID-gen path is correct.
